notes: READING A MONTH BACK, YOU CAN NOW TAKE THE REVERSED ENTRIES OUT. THE COMPLAINT. Look up a month in the General Ledger and the entries that were reversed are sitting there beside the entries that reversed them. Both halves are real and both belong in the audit trail, but reading the month back they pad the listing and inflate the Debit and Credit totals by the same amount twice over. HIDE REVERSED ENTRIES. A checkbox beside the date filters on the General Ledger, and beside the search box on Journal Vouchers. It takes out entries that were reversed AND the entries that reversed them. Both halves go together, and that is the whole design: hiding the original while leaving its reversal, or the other way round, would not tidy the extract, it would make it wrong by the amount of the entry, in the direction that shows money leaving the account that never left. It is a view, never a deletion, and it is OFF by default. Nothing disappears from a ledger unless you ask. IT TELLS YOU WHICH QUESTION IT ANSWERED. Two cases, and they are not the same. Both halves inside your dates: they already netted to nothing, so the totals do not move and all that goes is the noise, which is the case this exists for. One half outside your dates, a March entry reversed in June say: now the totals DO move, because the extract has stopped describing what March reported at the time and started describing what still stands today. The note under the filters says how many lines went, from how many vouchers, and how many of those vouchers were reversed outside the dates on screen. The printed page and the Excel export carry the same warning, because a filed extract that quietly omits entries, with nothing on the paper to say so, is the worst version of this. THE BALANCE COLUMN KEEPS UP. The balance brought forward is worked out on both bases at once, so the opening figure always matches the rows beneath it. Turn the toggle on over a period whose opening balance included an entry since reversed, and the opening moves with it. JOURNAL VOUCHERS HAS IT TOO. A reversed journal already carries a status pill there, and the search could already find them, but a search includes, it cannot exclude, and excluding is what reading a month back needs. On one real ledger 83 percent of that list was one half of a reversal, and for one month it was 64 of 64: every voucher on the screen, and not one of them a real entry. There are no totals on that list, so nothing there can be distorted. When everything on screen is a reversal half, the list says so rather than looking empty. ALSO FIXED: the search box, the record count and the toggles beside them on five screens sat in plain block flow because the toolbar that holds them was never given its styling. INSTALLING: no data changes. This installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
